newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas Q1 military earnings up.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas Q1 military earnings up.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said Thursday its operating earnings in the military aircraft segment were $259 million in the first quarter, up from $250 million in the year-ago quarter.
Earnings in the F/A-18E/F military airplane program increased, while results were lower from the F-15 and F/A-18C/D programs, it added.
McDonnell said it has received approval from the U.S. Department of Defense to begin production of the first 12 aircraft in the F/A-18E/F program.

The company said production cost increases, primarily on the F/A-18C/D and F-15 programs, hurt first quarter results in the segment. The phase-in of work after a 99-day strike at its St. Louis operations, which ended in September 1996, along with increased retirements of experienced personnel late in the year, impacted productivity, McDonnell added.
A build-up of the production rate on the F-15 added to increased production costs.
Military segment revenues in the first quarter were $1.9 billion, down from $2.0 billion in the 1996 quarter.

Operating earnings on the missiles, space and electronic systems segment in the first quarter fell to $36 million from $58 million. Expenditures for the Delta III launch vehicle under development and lower earnings on the Delta II program caused the decrease in earnings, McDonnell said.
Revenues for missiles, space and electronic systems were $553 million, dwon from $608 million.

Commercial aircraft operating earnings in the first quarter fell to $4 million from $19 million a year ago. Earnings from the sale of spare parts and related services contributed to earnings. Increased losses on the MD-95 program, currently in development, were partly offset by some reduction in cost estimates on prior deliveries of trijet and twin-jet aircraft.
Year-ago commercial aircraft results included an unspecified insurance recovery.
Revenues for commercial aircraft were $624 million, up from $428 million a year ago.

Operating earnings in the financial services and other segment were $22 million in the first quarter, up from $20 million a year ago. Revenues in this segment were $101 million, an increase of $14 million from a year ago.
